depends_on.name: owner_id
depends_on.documentation: The document this body holds the value of: a statement, or a standalone value document (a shared image, waveform or term list; item 20). The edge repeats (T15) when one body holds part of the value of several statements: a raw recording file is shared by the observations of every electrode recorded in it, each observation's channels named by its acquisition_channels_id (Jess Haley, 2026-10-21, did_v2_recording_observation_plan.md). A later body appends without rewriting the owner. Batch check `standalone_value` (report-only first; #73 audit 2 D13): when this names a value document, that document is a STANDALONE value -- not a statement, relation or clock_alignment leaf, all of which are also values. A `migration` document's report is its body too ([migration record], Jess Haley, 2026-11-01, did_v2_go_forward_class_audit.md: "the report as its body").

file.name: body_data
file.documentation: The byte payload, always a DID FILE SERIES (item 17): member `body_data_k` holds chunk k, numbered from 0; an unchunked body is one member, `body_data_0`. A file held OUTSIDE the database is a member recorded by location and not ingested (item 25).

fields.name: format
fields.documentation: Container format of the carried bytes, as a file-format term: EDAM format terms (e.g. EDAM:format_3591 TIFF, EDAM:format_3997 MPEG-4, EDAM:format_2333 binary), EMPTY where EDAM has none (OME-Zarr). NOT a file extension and NOT a media-type string (data_body plan sec.2, amended 2026-10-14). A descriptor only.

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: compression
fields.documentation: Compression applied within or around `format` (e.g. 'lzw', 'gzip'). Empty when the bytes are stored uncompressed.

fields.name: filename
fields.documentation: Original filename of the payload, if any.

fields.name: content_hash
fields.documentation: Optional hash of the payload bytes AS STORED in `body_data` -- after `compression`, not before. A natural dedup / integrity key, checkable without decoding. did_v1 source: `generic_file.checksum`, the 32-character lowercase MD5 ndi.fun.file.MD5 computes over the stored file. The algorithm is declared beside it, in `hash_algorithm`.

fields.name: notes
fields.documentation: Optional free text about the payload: V2's one free-text field, a last resort after every place a term can go ([one free-text field: notes], [notes on three classes], Jess Haley 2026-10-25, did_v2_go_forward_class_audit.md). Text a migration writes here keeps its labelled form (e.g. 'NGFF multiscales type "..."'). Was `description` until 2026-11-01.

fields.name: hash_algorithm
fields.documentation: The algorithm `content_hash` was computed with: MD5 | SHA-1 | SHA-256 | SHA-512. Without it a hash cannot be checked (item 25).

fields.name: size_bytes
fields.documentation: Size of the stored bytes. A cheap first identity check (item 25).

fields.name: file_created
fields.documentation: When the payload file was created, if the source recorded it. Named file_* so it is never confused with the document's own timestamp.

fields.name: file_modified
fields.documentation: When the payload file was last modified, if the source recorded it.

fields.name: redundant
fields.documentation: True = this body adds NO information beyond its owner's non-redundant body (e.g. a coarser zoom level of an image pyramid): an exact, deterministic rebuild exists, so it is safe to delete. That non-redundant body is its source -- no edge is needed, and the reason it is kept goes in `description` (T6 as amended by #73 audit 2 D6). Nothing may cite a redundant body as the only copy of a fact.

fields.name: conditions
fields.documentation: One-value facts true of every value in THIS body but not of every body of its owner (a reduced pyramid level's `summary statistic: maximum`; a lossy or preview copy). The same entry shape as `statement.conditions`. A fact true of every body belongs on the owner instead; a variable appears at most once across the owner's conditions and covariates and this body's (a batch check: the owner does not list its bodies). Each entry is {variable, unit, source_unit, approximate} plus exactly ONE value form -- `term`, `quantity` {value, source_value}, `count`, `text`, `logical` or `matrix` (a numeric N-D array, data_body AMENDMENT 4) -- the same entry as a covariate's, holding one value where a covariate holds one per position along its dimensions (2026-10-19; data_body plan AMENDMENT 6).

fields.name: variable
fields.documentation: The condition's name (arm direction, OD600, trial type); registry-keyed for its value_set (D9).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: unit
fields.documentation: Canonical unit of `quantity.value`, for the whole condition. Absent for a non-numeric value or a unitless number. A registered unit term (schemas/registry/did_v2_term_registry.json), the canonical unit of the variable's quantity: the list is tools/canonical_units.py, read by tools/check_term_registry.py (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [units bound]).

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: source_unit
fields.documentation: The unit the source gave the value in, as a term: the unit's registered term (schemas/registry/did_v2_term_registry.json), its label as the name (did_v2_source_unit_plan.md). Blank when the source gives no unit.

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: approximate
fields.documentation: Applies to the whole condition.

fields.name: term
fields.documentation: A categorical value: one term ({node, name}), or a LABEL ({name}, no node) when no term exists.

fields.name: node
fields.documentation: The CURIE (prefix resolved via CURIE_lookups_meta.json).

fields.name: name
fields.documentation: The human-readable label.

fields.name: quantity
fields.documentation: A numeric value, in `unit`, plus what the source wrote.

fields.name: value
fields.documentation: Canonical value, in `unit`.

fields.name: source_value
fields.documentation: As-recorded value, VERBATIM in `source_unit` (v1 writes a threshold as the string "0.030", and the string is kept).

fields.name: count
fields.documentation: An integer value.

fields.name: text
fields.documentation: A free-text value.

fields.name: logical
fields.documentation: A true/false value (Jess Haley 2026-10-22 [logical entries]): whether a setting was on, whether a condition held. One value form.

fields.name: matrix
fields.documentation: A numeric N-D array value, in `unit` (absent for unitless numbers): row-major as JSON nested arrays, every dimension written: an n x 3 palette is [[r, g, b], ...], one inner array per row, and a vector is written with its dimension as one row [[a, b, c]] or one column [[a], [b], [c]], never a flat [a, b, c], which cannot say which (data_body plan AMENDMENT 4, corrected 2026-10-21). The whole array is ONE value of the entry's `variable`; it is not split into entries. (data_body AMENDMENT 4, 2026-10-21.)
